name: Example: Stating the Definition of Non-Divisibility
problem:
Fill in the blanks so that the following reasoning is correct:

The notation $5 \not\mid 16$ means ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114596/assets/0bae0a5f51c3e76e064e79e0f84fca3d994ff54012f630d7dd2bc6a3ae02aa2e.svg) It is equivalent to the statement that for $\[6pt]$ ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114596/assets/61d9319f2a01d9cf62fd2a1701c6ebf2925774936b3a60bc687fb1c88f12a6ff.svg)
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114596/assets/05372931bea1e2d29016156cefebe65c770880362d078a4b3949aaadcabb6bf9.svg) we have ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114596/assets/9c35e9a87d5d59359ff108abaed0f1a9a3c51ff08eafbc30e177ce4e8c428d76.svg)
worked_solution:
The notation $a \not\mid b$ means $a$ does not divide $b.$ So, $5 \not\mid 16$ means ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114596/assets/6ec0f63f68ab4d8442da8966e85564948087e868f6e246fdc14526ff1767b4a1.svg)

According to the definition of integer divisibility, the fact that $a$ does not divide $b$ means that for any integer $k,$ we have that 

$$
b \neq a k.
$$

 

Therefore, $5 \not\mid 16$ is equivalent to the statement that for $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm{ any}}$ $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm{integer}}$ $k,$ we have $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}16 \neq 5k}.$
